         Scimitar Partners LP and Bar H Bar Land & Cattle Co. (collectively, “Bar H Bar Ranch

and Nature Preserve”) files this response to Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC (“Oncor”) and

LCRA Transmission Service Corporation (“LCRA”) (collectively, “Joint Applicants”) objections

to and motion to strike portions of the direct testimony of Michael D. Noonan. Further, Bar H Bar

Ranch and Nature Preserve object to both Joint Applicants’ objections to and motion to strike Mr.

Noonan’s direct testimony as untimely for failure to comply with State Office of Administrative

Hearings (“SOAH”) Order Nos. 1 and 6.

              I.        OBJECTIONS TO AND MOTION TO DISMISS JOINT APPLICANT’S
                        OBJECTIONS TO AND MOTION TO STRIKE AS UNTIMELY FOR
                          FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH SOAH ORDER NOS. 1 AND 6


           Pursuant to SOAH Order No. 6, parties had until 5:00 PM CT on May 18, 2026, to object

to intervenor direct testimony. Further, SOAH Order No. 1 makes clear that though interchange

service is acceptable in most instances, “an exception applies to discovery requests, responses to

discovery requests, motions, responses to motions, and other filings that request or require

action by another party, which must be emailed to the party that is the target of the filing.” 1 Both

an objection to direct testimony and a motion to strike direct testimony would fall squarely under

this exception in SOAH Order No. 1. Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve will note that neither

Mr. Parish nor Mr. Reeder were served a copy of those objections and motion to strike until four

(4) calendar days after the deadline to object to or move to strike intervenor testimony. While Bar

H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve would like to chalk it up to an accidental oversight on the part

of the Joint Applicants, the Joint Applicants’ own certificate of service seems to dispute the

possibility of this. In their objections to and motion to strike Mr. Noonan’s direct testimony, the

Joint Applicants’ state “a copy of this document has been filed with the Commission and served

on all parties of record via the PUC Interchange.” 2 This seems to indicate that Joint Applicants had

no intention of emailing a copy of the objections and motion to strike to counsel for Bar H Bar

Ranch and Nature Preserve. Counsel for Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve instead had to

reach out to counsel for Joint Applicants on May 22, 2026 asking why they had not been served,

and a few hours later received an email from a representative of one of the law firms representing

the deadline and only after counsel for Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve alerted Joint

Applicants to this failure to provide notice is not a cure to a violation of the order.

         Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve will note there is a fairness issue and power

imbalance inherent in these proceedings. Oncor is the largest utility in the state with billions in

revenues who has an ample supply of experienced lawyers and regulatory specialists at its disposal,

funded out of its Commission-approved rates, to assist in these proceedings. LCRA similarly is a

large utility with a substantial number of experienced lawyers and regulatory specialists able to

assist in these proceedings. Each have sponsored countless CCN proceedings over decades’ time.

Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve is a family ranch and nature preserve who only has two

attorneys and a limited budget. If anyone should be held to the strictest standard of following the

rules and SOAH’s orders it should be the Joint Applicants who have endless resources to throw at

intervenors including with these objections and motion to strike. Luckily for Bar H Bar Ranch and

Nature Preserve, its counsel via their own diligence was able to eventually catch that objections

had been levied on their witness but for many intervenors they might not even know that the Joint

Applicants have objected to or moved to strike portions of their testimony. But if the ALJs do not

enforce the rules’ time requirements, Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve’s time for preparing a

suitable response to this motion seeking to exclude portions of our direct testimony will be severely

compressed, which is exactly what the Commission’s rule aims to avoid. For fairness

considerations rooted in affording parties the due process of ensuring that the applicant utilities

             ii.    Non-Expert Opinion

           Joint Applicants claim that the testimony of Michael D. Noonan is non-expert testimony

and claim that Mr. Noonan does not meet the standard under Texas Rules of Evidence 702 to be

qualified as an expert witness. Joint Applicants cite to case law which states that the party offering

expert testimony bears the burden to prove qualification under Rule 702 and must demonstrate that

the witness "possesses special knowledge as to the very matter on which he proposes to give an

opinion."5 We agree that Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature Preserve does bear the burden to prove that

Mr. Noonan is an expert witness but have far exceeded the bar under Rule 702 to prove that.

           Texas Rules of Evidence 702 states that “[a] witness who is qualified as an expert by

knowledge, skill, experience, training, or education may testify in the form of an opinion or

otherwise if the expert’s scientific, technical, or other specialized knowledge will help the trier of

fact to understand the evidence or to determine a fact in issue.”

           Let’s look at Mr. Noonan’s qualifications to assess his credentials. Mr. Noonan stated that

he “began working full-time in the land rights and permitting space in 1982.” Further he has served

as Director of Right-of-Way (“ROW”), Siting, and Land Rights for two national engineering firms,

Westwood Professional Services, Inc. and HDR Engineering. Lastly, he currently is President of

designated as such in this proceeding.

knowledge of the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (“USPAP”) and has

ground is really just argument in the guise of an objection, as we discuss below.

           Further, it seems Joint Applicants are trying to force intervenors, with limited budgets to

fight for their property rights, to hire multiple experts with very specific qualifications just to

submit evidence contrary to the Joint Applicants’ case and have their voices heard. Clearly, Mr.

Noonan has experience in the area in which he is testifying and does not need to be a licensed

appraiser to give an industry standard approach, and best practice, to the severance and bifurcation

issue along with an estimated valuation of damages to the property.

           We also note that Joint Applicants seem to be throwing stones from a glass house in their

in land valuation which is required to determine said costs. 12 In fact, from testimony alone, Mr.

Noonan appears to be substantially more qualified than Ms. Cooley to testify as to cost and we

of it. Further, this is not a jury trial and the SOAH ALJs have extensive expertise in this type of

proceeding and can give Mr. Noonan’s statements the appropriate weight necessary based upon

their own evaluation of it. For this reason, we urge the SOAH ALJs to overrule the objection to

                   b. Objected EMF Testimony

         Joint Applicants’ confusing objection to Attachment MDN-11 to Mr. Noonan’s testimony

offers no apparent grounds to support the objection. This Attachment consists of the Direct

Testimony of W Ben Johnson submitted to the Minnesota PUC, on EMF issues. All Joint

be stricken in its entirety, but their reference to page 11 of Mr. Noonan’s testimony provides no

testimony they would like stricken in page 11 as it involves both testimony related to Dr. Johnson

and electromagnetic fields (“EMF”) and effects on habitable structures more generally. Again,

           Nevertheless, we will respond to both the possible striking of portions of page 11 to Mr.

Noonan’s direct testimony as well as Exhibit MDN-11. First, as has already been covered

extensively in this pleading, Mr. Noonan is an expert in transmission line ROW, siting, and land

rights. Further, he has 44 years of experience in the field and has testified before many state

agencies including three previous times before the PUCT. Per Texas Rules of Evidence 703, an

expert witness “may base an opinion on facts or data in the case that the expert has been made

aware of, reviewed, or personally observed. If experts in the particular field would reasonably rely

on those kinds of facts or data in forming an opinion on the subject, they need not be admissible

for the opinion to be admitted.” Here, Mr. Noonan is discussing something he is clearly an expert

the SOAH ALJs and ultimately the Commission can assign Mr. Noonan’s testimony on setbacks

for habitable structures due to EMF as well as Exhibit MDN-11 the necessary weight it is entitled.

We therefore urge the SOAH ALJs to overrule the Joint Applicants’ objections and deny their

motion to strike.

              iii.   Relevance

            Joint Applicants next objected to the following statement in the direct testimony of Mr.

Noonan on relevance grounds:

                     "A definitive statement of the diminution of value and damages to the subject

            property, and associated costs, would need to be determined by a licensed appraiser with

            experience in these fields of analysis. However, based on my working knowledge and

            oversight of appraisal regiments adhering to the USPAP on similar takings, it is reasonable

            to assume damages to the remainder and loss of use on the subject property in the tens of

            millions of dollars."15

            The bar for relevance under the Texas Rules of Evidence 401 is that evidence is relevant

if: “(a) it has any tendency to make a fact more or less probable than it would be without the

            Joint Applicants have grossly misstated the Commission preliminary order. The

preliminary order actually says the following:

            “The Commission does not have the authority to adjudicate or set the amount of

            compensation for rights-of-way or for condemnation.”18

That is a very limited scope of what cannot be addressed by the Commission and only relates to

the Commission setting the actual value of compensation for ROW or condemnation. Put another

way, the Commission cannot as part of this proceeding say that Bar H Bar Ranch and Nature

controlling in a condemnation proceeding. Mr. Noonan is not asking the Commission to adjudicate
